old_note: *And after it is consummated, Beliar will descend, the great angel, the king of this world, which he has ruled ever since it came into being; and he will descend from his firmament in the form of a man, a king of unrighteousness, a slayer of his mother — this is the king of this world.* Ascension of Isaiah 4:2 names Beliar as *the king of this world,* the figure who has ruled it from the beginning. Matt 4:8-9's offer of *all the kingdoms of the world* by the devil is the same king-of-this-world figure offering what he currently administers. The Hebrew library's framework — Beliar / the devil as the temporary king-of-this-world during the present age (under Watcher-rebellion administration) — locks the framework reading that the wilderness-offer was not an empty bluff.
new_note: *Again, the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;* (Matthew 4:8). *After it is consummated, Beliar the great ruler, the king of this world, will descend, who hath ruled it since it came into being; yea, he will descent from his firmament in the likeness of a man, a lawless king, the slayer of his mother: who himself (even) this king.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:2). The Ascension of Isaiah says that Beliar is the king of this world and has ruled it since it came into being. When the devil takes Yahusha (Jesus) up the mountain and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, he is showing what he holds for the present age, so the offer that follows was no empty boast. But the same passage speaks of the completion of the world, and a rule that was given for a season is a rule with an end.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 4:2 — *Beliar the great ruler, the king of this world, will descend, who hath ruled it since it came into being.* The Ascension of Isaiah names the one who has ruled this world from the beginning, and the devil offers Yahusha (Jesus) what he holds.
drafter_flag: Live text of 4:2 carries a misprint, 'he will descent' (for 'descend'); quoted exactly as it stands. Old note quoted a different wording of the verse than the live text and used the phrases 'the Hebrew library' and 'Watcher-rebellion administration', which I dropped.

old_note: *And much power will be in his hands, and he will make all do what he chooses; and he will speak as the Beloved and will say: I am Elohim (God), and before me there was none. And all the people in the world will believe in him.* Ascension 4:9 names Beliar's standing worship-grab pattern — speaking as the Beloved, claiming the worship due to Elohim. Matt 4:9's *if thou wilt fall down and worship me* is the king-of-this-world enacting the same worship-grab at the Messianic level. The Hebrew library names the architecture; the gospel narrates one instance of it.
new_note: *And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.* (Matthew 4:9). *And they will sacrifice to him and they will serve him saying: "This is Elohim (God) and beside him there is no other." And they greater number of those who shall have been associated together in order to receive the Beloved, he will turn aside after him.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:8–9). Satan asks Yahusha (Jesus) for worship, and Yahusha (Jesus) refuses. The Ascension of Isaiah shows what the same ruler gets from the world in the days of the end: sacrifice and service, and the cry that there is no other god beside him, and then the greater number of those gathered to receive the Beloved turned aside after him. It is the same grab for worship, once refused by the Son in the wilderness, and then carried out on the many who do not hold fast.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 4:9 — *those who shall have been associated together in order to receive the Beloved, he will turn aside after him.* The ruler who asked the Son for worship turns aside the greater number of those gathered to receive the Beloved.
drafter_flag: Live text of 4:9 has a misprint, 'And they greater number' (for 'the'); quoted exactly. I quoted 4:8 with it because the worship the verse is about is in 4:8. Old note quoted wording from earlier in chapter 4 (the ruler speaking as the Beloved and saying he is Elohim), not 4:9; I kept its point (the worship grab) and anchored it on what 4:8 to 4:9 says.

old_note: *Beliar was wroth with Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) because of his vision, and because of the unmasking with which he had unmasked Sammael, and because by him the going forth of the Beloved from the seventh heaven had been made known.* Ascension 1:3 names Beliar's adversarial pattern toward the prophetic revelation of the Beloved's descent. Matt 4:10's *Get thee hence, Satan* sends the same Beliar-figure away in the same architecture: the Beloved who has descended dismisses the king-of-this-world who opposes the descent.
new_note: *Then saith Yahusha (Jesus) unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God), and him only shalt thou serve.* (Matthew 4:10). *For Beliar was in great wrath against Isaiah by reason of the vision, and because of the exposure wherewith he had exposed Sammael, and because through him the going forth of the Beloved from the seventh heaven had been made known, and His transformation and His descent and the likeness into which He should be transformed (that is) the likeness of man, and the persecution wherewith he should be persecuted, and the torturers wherewith the children of Yashar'el (Israel) should torture Him, and the coming of His twelve disciples, and the teaching, and that He should before the sabbath be crucified upon the tree, and should be crucified together with wicked men, and that He should be buried in the sepulchre,* (Ascension of Isaiah 3:13). Beliar's rage against Isaiah is over one thing: the prophet had made known the Beloved's going forth from the seventh heaven and his descent in the likeness of man. In the wilderness the same adversary meets the Beloved now come down in that likeness, and is sent away with the commandment of Torah: worship Yahuah (the Lord) and serve him only. The one Beliar tried to keep hidden dismisses him with the Word.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 3:13 — *the going forth of the Beloved from the seventh heaven had been made known.* The Beloved whose descent enraged Beliar sends Satan away with the Torah's own word.
drafter_flag: Re-pointed from 1:3 to 3:13 — the verse the old note quoted (Beliar's wrath at the revealing of the Beloved); 1:3 is the list of judgments and powers. Live 3:13 text is long and is quoted whole, as the rule requires.

old_note: *Love one another in deed, and in word, and in the inclination of the soul. For in the presence of my father I spake peaceably to Joseph; and when I had gone out, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.* Testament of Gad 2:2 (DB ch 62) names the spirit-of-hatred-to-the-act-of-murder architecture in the patriarch's own testimony — the heart-root that the Torah always taught the murder-commandment named. Matt 5:22's *whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment* walks the same Hebrew library architecture at the antithesis-restoration level: the oral tradition stopped at the bodily act; the Torah and the testaments and the Beatitudes name the heart-substance the act follows from.
new_note: *But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.* (Matthew 5:22). *For in the presence of my father I spake peaceably to Joseph; and when I had gone out, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:2). Gad is speaking to his sons about what he did to Joseph. In front of their father he spoke peaceably, and the moment he had gone out hatred darkened his mind and drove his soul toward killing his brother. That is the road Yahusha (Jesus) is describing: the commandment against murder was never only about the hand, because anger at a brother is where the killing begins. He is not setting the Torah aside but reading the commandment down to its root, the same root Gad learned the hard way and warned his children about.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:2 — *the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.* Gad confesses that hatred began as a darkened mind and ended in a plan to kill, which is the very path Yahusha (Jesus) traces back to anger.
drafter_flag: Old citation (Testament of Gad 2:2) was stale; card sits on the right verse, now cited by the live numbering. Old note quoted the previous verse inside the italics; I quote only 100:2.

old_note: *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, cast forth the poison of hate and speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile.* Testament of Gad 2:3 (DB ch 62) names the love-replacing-hatred ethic at the heart level — *cast forth the poison of hate and speak peaceably.* Matt 5:44's *love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you* walks the same Hebrew library ethic at the Sermon level. The antithesis is not a Yahusha (Jesus) innovation against Mosheh (Moses); the love-of-the-personal-enemy ethic was already taught in the patriarch's own testimony to his sons.
new_note: *But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;* (Matthew 5:44). *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile; and if he repent and confess, forgive him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3). Gad does not stop at loving the brother who treats you well. If a man sins against you, speak peaceably to him, keep no guile in your soul, and forgive him when he repents. Yahusha (Jesus) reaches the same place from the other side, telling us to bless those who curse us, do good to those who hate us, and pray for those who persecute us. This is not a teaching set against Moses; the fathers were already handing it to their sons, and Gad hands it down out of what hatred did to Joseph.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3 — *if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile.* Gad tells his sons to answer a brother's wrong with peace and forgiveness, which is the same heart Yahusha (Jesus) asks for toward an enemy.
drafter_flag: Old note quoted 'cast forth the poison of hate', which is not in the live 100:3 (the poison language belongs to the next verse, 100:4); I quote only what 100:3 says. Citation moved from stale 'Gad 2:3' to live 100:3.

old_note: *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon them...* 2 Baruch 35:1 names the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic-harvest architecture explicitly — the harvest comes when the time of the age has ripened; the harvest is of evil-and-good-seeds together. Matt 9:37's *the harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few* walks the same architecture at the King's arrival: the harvest the apocalyptic-stream had named as eschatologically-future is now plenteous and present at the King's seeing of the multitudes.
new_note: *Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;* (Matthew 9:37). *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.* (2 Baruch 70:2). Baruch looks ahead to the time when the age has ripened and the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, and the Mighty One brings bewilderment on the earth and its rulers. Yahusha (Jesus), looking at the crowds, says the harvest truly is plenteous, and the labourers are few. What Baruch placed at the end of the age, Yahusha (Jesus) says is already at hand. Both speak of a harvest of two kinds of seed, which is why the sorting matters and why labourers are wanted.
member_note: 2 Baruch 70:2 — *the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come.* The harvest of the age, evil and good seeds together, is the harvest Yahusha (Jesus) says is already plenteous.
drafter_flag: Old note cited 2 Baruch 35:1 (stale numbering); the quoted words are in the live 2 Baruch 70:2, and the card sits on 70:2. The 'good and evil seeds' read as the two kinds sown together until harvest; no further claim made.

old_note: *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon them...* 2 Baruch 35:1 — the same eschatological-harvest-of-the-age verse also anchors Matt 9:38's *pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers.* The Lord-of-the-harvest is the Mighty One the apocalyptic-stream had named; the labourers being prayed-for are about to be commissioned at Matt 10:1.
new_note: *Pray ye therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.* (Matthew 9:38) *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.* (2 Baruch 70:2) Yahusha (Jesus) sees the crowds and tells his disciples to ask Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest for labourers, because the harvest is standing ready. Baruch had already been told what that harvest is: the time of the age ripens, and what was sown in it, evil seed and good seed alike, has come up. The one Baruch calls the Mighty One is the owner of that field, so the prayer in Matthew is a prayer prayed inside that ripening time, and the next chapter sends the twelve out as the answer.
member_note: 2 Baruch 70:2 — *the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come.* The prayer Yahusha (Jesus) teaches in Matthew 9:38 asks for workers for this same harvest.
drafter_flag: Old note cited this verse as 2 Baruch 35:1 (stale numbering) and its quote trailed off; card is already on 70:2, citation fixed. Old note's word 'them' differs from live 'the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers'; quoted live text.

old_note: *And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* 2 Baruch 38:4 names the twelve-tribes-bound-by-one-bond architecture in the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic register — all the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, born from one father. The framework's gathering-thesis holds the twelve-tribe-restoration as the load-bearing prophetic substance; Matt 9:36's *sheep having no shepherd* multitudes are the same twelve-tribe-bound-by-one-bond body the wisdom-stream had named.
new_note: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) *And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* (2 Baruch 78:3) Yahusha (Jesus) looks at the multitudes and finds them scattered and without a shepherd, which is a picture of a people and not of a crowd of strangers. Baruch writes to the brethren in captivity and says who that people is: the twelve tribes, bound by one bond because they are born from one father. However far they have been carried, they are one flock by birth, and that is what moves Yahusha (Jesus) to compassion.
member_note: 2 Baruch 78:3 — *all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* The scattered, shepherdless multitudes Yahusha (Jesus) sees in Matthew 9:36 are this one family born from one father.
drafter_flag: Old note cited 2 Baruch 38:4 (stale numbering); fixed to the live 78:3.

old_note: *He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* 2 Baruch 38:7 (epistle to the nine-and-a-half scattered tribes across the Euphrates) names the wisdom-stream's gathering-of-the-dispersed-with-much-mercy architecture explicitly. The much-mercy register at 2 Baruch 38:7 is the same mercy-substance Hosea 6:6 names at Matt 9:13; the gathering-of-the-dispersed IS the mercy-architecture of the kingdom-at-hand.
new_note: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) *For if ye so do these things, He will continually remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* (2 Baruch 78:7) Yahusha (Jesus) is moved with compassion at sheep scattered abroad with no shepherd. Baruch closes his letter to the scattered tribes with the promise that answers it: Yahuah (Lord) will never forget or forsake them, and with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed. The compassion in Matthew and the mercy in Baruch are one mercy, and its work is the gathering.
member_note: 2 Baruch 78:7 — *with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* The compassion Yahusha (Jesus) shows the scattered sheep in Matthew 9:36 is this promised mercy at work.
drafter_flag: Old note cited 2 Baruch 38:7 (stale numbering) and tied it to Hosea 6:6 at Matthew 9:13; I dropped the Hosea link because no live text for it was given to quote. Citation fixed to 78:7.

old_note: *Will persecute the plant which the Twelve Apostles of the Beloved have planted. Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.* The Ascension of Isaiah 4:3 (in the Belial-prediction at the chapter's mid-section) names the wisdom-stream's prophetic-witness to the twelve-apostles-with-one-betrayer architecture explicitly — the plant the Twelve plant will be persecuted; one of the Twelve will be delivered into the hand of the persecutor. Matt 10:4's Yahudah (Judah) Iscariot listed-with-betrayal-note and Matt 10:16-22's persecution-disclosure walk the same architecture at the commissioning-discourse register. The framework reads the Ascension passage as the wisdom-stream's confirmation that the inner-circle-betrayal and the persecution-of-the-plant are not surprise-developments but architecture-elements named in advance.
new_note: *Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.* (Matthew 10:4). *Will persecute the plant which the Twelve Apostles of the Beloved have planted. Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:3). Before the Twelve are ever named, the Ascension of Isaiah says that the ruler of this world will persecute what they plant and that one of the Twelve will fall into his hands. Matthew's list of the apostles closes on exactly that note, with the last name carrying the word betrayed. Nothing in the account takes the Beloved by surprise. The persecution of the plant and the loss of one from the inner circle were spoken of ahead of time, and Matthew's commissioning of the Twelve goes on to warn them of what is coming.
member_note: Ascension of Isaiah 4:3 — *Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.* The persecution of the plant and the loss of one of the Twelve were told in advance, and Matthew's list ends on the one who betrayed.
drafter_flag: Old note's phrase list (wisdom-stream, architecture elements) removed. 4:3 begins mid-sentence in the live text ('Will persecute...'); its subject is the ruler of 4:2.

old_note: *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him.* Testament of Gad 62:3 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the heart-substance + the speak-peaceably-to-the-sinning-brother substance the King's chapter-arc lands-on at v.35 and operationalizes at vv.15-17. The framework reads the verse against the unforgiving-servant parable + the assembly-discipline procedure. The Testament-of-Gad's confessional-instruction — Gad confessing his-own-hatred-of-Joseph and the substance-of-repentance he-came-to — names the heart-substance the King's *from your hearts* (v.35) requires. The framework reads this as the wisdom-stream's direct prefiguring of both ends of the chapter-arc: (a) the v.15 first-step *go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone* operates from the substance Testament of Gad names — *speak peaceably to him*; (b) the v.35 chapter-closing *if ye from your hearts forgive not* operates from the substance Testament of Gad names — *love ye one another from the heart.* The wisdom-stream had carried the heart-substance; the King's assembly-architecture institutionalizes the heart-substance at the kingdom-citizens' corporate-register.
new_note: *So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.* (Matthew 18:35). *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile; and if he repent and confess, forgive him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3). Yahusha (Jesus) closes His warning with the words from your hearts: the Father will deal with us as we deal with a brother we will not forgive. Gad gives his sons the same measure. Love one another from the heart, speak peaceably to a brother who sins against you, and when he repents and confesses, forgive him. Both put the whole matter in the heart, where a brother is either forgiven or kept in the ledger.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3 — *Love ye one another from the heart.* Gad's call to love from the heart and forgive the repentant brother stands behind the warning that closes Yahusha's (Jesus's) teaching on forgiveness.
drafter_flag: Old note cited stale 'Testament of Gad 62:3' and leaned on Matthew 18:15-17 and the unforgiving-servant parable, neither of which is on this card; I kept the one true link (from the heart, forgive the brother) and cited by live numbering.

old_note: *Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, that ye may have it as a treasure in heaven.* Testaments XII Levi 7 (chapter 18 in the corpus enumeration) verse 5 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the *treasure in heaven* substance — the exact phrase the King restates at Matt 19:21's *thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.* The framework reads this as the wisdom-stream's most-direct verbal-prefiguration of the King's-substance. The Levi-testament-substance had named the architecture: *work righteousness... that ye may have it as a treasure in heaven.* The kingdom-citizens' substance is righteousness-walked-on-the-earth that-translates-into-treasure-in-heaven; the substance is in continuity with the apostolic-restatement at 1 Timothy 6:18-19's *that they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate; laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come.* The King at Matt 19:21 stands on the wisdom-stream-substance the Test XII Levi 7 had named. The framework reads this in continuity with the FRAMEWORK-MAJOR substance the King ties to the kingdom-entry-criterion at v.17 — *keep the commandments* — and the diagnostic-test at v.21 the heart-Torah-substance lands on. The wisdom-stream, the King, and the apostle all hold the same substance: righteousness-walked + treasure-in-heaven are one architecture.
new_note: *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.* (Matthew 19:21) *Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 29:5) Yahusha (Jesus) tells the rich young man that if he wants to be perfect he should go, sell what he has, give to the poor, and have treasure in heaven, and then come and follow. Levi tells his sons the same thing in other words: work righteousness on the earth, and it is kept as a treasure in heaven. Just before this, Yahusha (Jesus) had told the man that the way into life is to keep the commandments, so the treasure in heaven is what righteousness done on the earth is laid up as.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 29:5 — *Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven.* Levi's call to work righteousness on the earth and have it as a treasure in heaven is the word Yahusha (Jesus) speaks in Matthew 19:21.
drafter_flag: Old note cited this as Levi 7 verse 5 / chapter 18 (stale); fixed to 29:5. Also tied to 1 Timothy 6:18–19; dropped since no live text was given to quote.

old_note: *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth, and likewise also the three.* Testaments XII Joseph 15 (chapter 86 in the corpus enumeration) verse 2 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the twelve-harts-feeding-then-dispersed substance — the same scattering-and-restoration-of-the-twelve-tribes architecture the King at Matt 19:28's *judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)* presupposes-as-the-completed-gathering-architecture. The framework reads the verse against the King's-statement. The Joseph-testament-substance names the substance directly: twelve-harts (the twelve-tribes) feeding-together-originally, then-dispersed (the nine = the ten-northern-tribes; the three = the southern-house-substance), the substance the prophets had named at Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 37:15-22's two-sticks-becoming-one. The substance the King-states at Matt 19:28 is the gathering-and-judging-substance the wisdom-stream-Joseph-testament had named the architecture-for. The wisdom-stream, the Tanakh-prophets, and the King's-mouth all hold the same architecture: twelve-tribes-dispersed-and-gathered-and-judged-by-twelve-apostles-at-the-consummated-substance. The framework reads in framework-substance per Red Line #11 — the twelve-tribes are LITERAL twelve-tribes, the paternal-blood remnant the Father-promised-through-the-prophets-and-now-states-at-the-King's-mouth. FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.
new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth, and likewise also the three.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 129:2). Joseph sees twelve harts feeding together, and all twelve end up dispersed over the earth, the nine first and the three likewise. The twelve harts read as the twelve tribes, scattered. Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of those same tribes as a whole people sitting under judgment when the Son of Adam takes His throne, with twelve thrones set for judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). A people who are to be judged as twelve tribes must first be gathered as twelve, and Joseph's vision is the scattering that the gathering answers.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 129:2 — *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth.* Joseph's vision of twelve harts dispersed over the earth is the scattering that Yahusha (Jesus) assumes when He speaks of judging the twelve tribes.
drafter_flag: Old note said the nine are the ten northern tribes and the three are the southern house. Nine is not ten and three is not two, so I did not carry that identification; I say only what the verse says (twelve dispersed, nine first, then the three). Old citation ('Joseph 15', 'chapter 86') was stale; live 129:2 used.

old_note: *And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.* Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 94:5 (Testament of Benjamin 9) names THE direct extras-stream verbal-anchor for the lowly-on-earth-and-glorious-in-heaven substance — the precise architecture the King names at Matt 20:28's *the Son of Adam came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.* The framework reads the verse as the most-direct pseudepigraphal-anchor for the kenotic-incarnational architecture the King articulates at the chapter-pivot. The Tanakh-Suffering-Servant-substance the King draws-from at v.28 (Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 53:3's *despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows*; 53:5-6's *wounded for our transgressions ... Yahuah (the LORD) hath laid on him the iniquity of us all*; 53:10-12's *make his soul an offering for sin ... bare the sin of many*) is the same lowly-on-earth substance Testaments 94:5 names; the eschatological-glorious-in-heaven substance the wisdom-stream points-forward-to is the same substance 1 Enoch 62's Son-of-Adam-on-the-throne-of-his-glory names. The framework reads this in continuity with Philippians 2:6-11's *made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant ... wherefore Elohim (God) also hath highly exalted him* — the apostolic-witness restates the substance the King's-own-mouth named at the gospel-pivot and the wisdom-and-pseudepigraphal-stream named at the prefiguring-register.
new_note: *Even as the Son of Adam came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.* (Matthew 20:28). *And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5). Yahusha (Jesus) says of Himself that the Son of Adam came not to be served but to serve, and to give His life a ransom for many. Benjamin, looking ahead, says he knows how lowly He will be upon the earth and how glorious in heaven. The lowliness and the glory belong to one person: the one who takes the servant's place on earth is the one who ascends from Hades into heaven.

new_note: *And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.* (Matthew 27:35). *And the god of that world will stretch forth his hand against the Son, and they will crucify Him on a tree, and will slay Him not knowing who He is.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:14). The Ascension of Isaiah puts the weight where it belongs. The one who stretches out his hand against the Son is the god of that world, the adversary behind the deed, and those who carry it out do so not knowing who He is. Matthew then tells it as it happened, that they crucified him and divided his garments, in keeping with what the prophet had said. The tree is the place of the curse that falls on a people for breaking the covenant, and the Son took that curse on himself, so that the scattered might come home to the Torah, not away from it.

new_note: *Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.* (Matthew 27:50). *And when He hath plundered the angel of death, He will ascend on the third day, and he will remain in that world five hundred and forty-five days.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:16). new_note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52). *And then many of the righteous will ascend with Him, whose spirits do not receive their garments till Yahuah (Lord) Messiah (Christ) ascend and they ascend with Him.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:17).
